items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] It sounds like...Several good players have gotten stuck in places like that, like Carl Fontana, James Moody, for a number of years.

ctx.x: Somewhat, because what happened after that, I felt like...I was having a problem getting a job. Not just a job. I could have...and I've had some people talk to me strictly private, even a union official: 'Monk, you know you're really liked here. It will be no problem that you can get a job in one of these showrooms.' And I said, 'Man, that ain't playing. It's not playing. Sorry, but I haven't retired. I want to play.' I want to express myself. That's what playing was for me.
It sounds like...Several good players have gotten stuck in places like that, like Carl Fontana, James Moody, for a number of years.

Right. And I just didn't have any reason to do that. I don't have any babies or anything, that kind of responsibility. Like guys that have got their wife and kids and they got to do this, and they got to work at the post office and got to do these things. I didn't have them kind of commitments, that I had to go do that for them.
